drivingQuestion: What mourning rites, if any, are observed for a deceased slave or maidservant?
outcomeNote: the baraitot and R' Eliezer's conduct establish that no mourning rites are observed for slaves; the sages' difficulty against R' Yosei's eulogy is left standing without reply

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין עוֹמְדִין עֲלֵיהֶם בְּשׁוּרָה, וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים עֲלֵיהֶם בִּרְכַּת אֲבֵלִים וְתַנְחוּמֵי אֲבֵלִים.
segments.en: «The Sages» taught in a baraita: For «slaves and maidservants» who die, «one does not stand in a row» of comforters to console the mourners, «and one recites neither the blessing of the mourners nor the consolation of the mourners.»

segments.he: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵתָה שִׁפְחָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. נִכְנְסוּ תַּלְמִידָיו לְנַחֲמוֹ. כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה אוֹתָם עָלָה לַעֲלִיָּיה, וְעָלוּ אַחֲרָיו. נִכְנַס לָאַנְפִּילוֹן, נִכְנְסוּ אַחֲרָיו. נִכְנַס לַטְּרַקְלִין, נִכְנְסוּ אַחֲרָיו. אָמַר לָהֶם: כִּמְדוּמֶּה אֲנִי שֶׁאַתֶּם נִכְוִים בְּפוֹשְׁרִים, עַכְשָׁיו אִי אַתֶּם נִכְוִים אֲפִילּוּ בְּחַמֵּי חַמִּין, לֹא כָּךְ שָׁנִיתִי לָכֶם: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין עוֹמְדִים עֲלֵיהֶם בְּשׁוּרָה, וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים עֲלֵיהֶם בִּרְכַּת אֲבֵלִים וְלֹא תַּנְחוּמֵי אֲבֵלִים? אֶלָּא מָה אוֹמְרִים עֲלֵיהֶם? — כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לוֹ לְאָדָם עַל שׁוֹרוֹ וְעַל חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁמֵּתוּ — ״הַמָּקוֹם יְמַלֵּא לְךָ חֶסְרוֹנְךָ״, כָּךְ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ עַל עַבְדּוֹ וְעַל שִׁפְחָתוֹ ״הַמָּקוֹם יְמַלֵּא לְךָ חֶסְרוֹנְךָ״.
segments.en: «An incident» is related that when «Rabbi Eliezer’s maidservant died, his students entered to console him. When he saw them» approaching «he went up to the second floor, and they went up after him. He entered the gatehouse [anpilon], and they entered after him. He entered the banquet hall [teraklin],» and «they entered after him.» Having seen them follow him everywhere, «he said to them: It seems to me that you would be burned by lukewarm water,» meaning that you could take a hint and when I went up to the second floor, you would understand that I did not wish to receive your consolations. «Now» I see that «you are not even burned by boiling hot water. Did I not teach you the following:» For «slaves and maidservants» who die, «one does not stand in a row» of comforters to console the mourners, «and one neither recites the blessing of the mourners nor» does he recite «the consolation of the mourners,» as the relationship between master and slave is not like a familial relationship? «Rather, what does one say about them» when they die? «Just as we say to a person about his ox or donkey which died: May the Omnipresent replenish your loss, so too do we say for one’s slave or maidservant» who died: «May the Omnipresent replenish your loss,» as the connection between a master and his slave is only financial in nature.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין מַסְפִּידִין אוֹתָן. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִם עֶבֶד כָּשֵׁר הוּא — אוֹמְרִים עָלָיו: ״הוֹי אִישׁ טוֹב וְנֶאֱמָן וְנֶהֱנֶה מִיגִיעוֹ״. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, מָה הִנַּחְתָּ לַכְּשֵׁרִים?
segments.en: «It was taught in another» baraita: «One does not eulogize slaves and maidservants. Rabbi Yosei says: If he was a virtuous servant, one recites over him» a eulogy of sorts: «Alas, a good and loyal man who enjoyed» the fruits «of his hard labor. They said to him: If so, what» praise «have you left for virtuous» Jews? A Jewish person would be proud to be eulogized in that manner.

moves.summary: a baraita: no row of comforters and no mourners' blessing or consolation for slaves and maidservants — qualifying the mishna's report that Rabban Gamliel accepted condolences for Tavi
moves.about: a baraita: for slaves and maidservants one does not stand in the row of comforters nor recite the mourners' blessing or consolation

moves.cueHe: מעשה ומתה שפחתו של רבי אליעזר
moves.summary: incident: R' Eliezer's maidservant died; his students came to console him and he withdrew from room to room while they followed
moves.about: when R' Eliezer's maidservant died he withdrew from room to room to evade his students' condolences

moves.cueHe: אמר להם: כמדומה אני שאתם נכוים בפושרים
moves.summary: R' Eliezer reproaches the students for missing his hint and reminds them that he taught them no row or mourners' blessing is made for slaves
moves.about: R' Eliezer reproaches his students for not taking the hint that he would not accept condolences for a maidservant

moves.summary: R' Eliezer asks: what then does one say over a dead slave?
moves.about: R' Eliezer adduces the rule he had taught them, that no row and no mourners' blessing or consolation is made for slaves and maidservants

moves.cueHe: כשם שאומרים לו לאדם על שורו ועל חמורו
moves.summary: as over a dead ox or donkey: 'may the Omnipresent replenish your loss'
another baraita: slaves and maidservants are not eulogized
moves.about: another baraita: slaves and maidservants are not eulogized, with R' Yosei's qualification and the sages' reply

moves.summary: R' Yosei: over a virtuous slave one says 'alas, a good and loyal man who enjoyed the fruit of his labor'
moves.about: whether a virtuous slave is eulogized at all: the first tanna says slaves are not eulogized, R' Yosei allows 'alas, a good and loyal man who enjoyed the fruit of his labor'

moves.summary: the sages: if so, what praise have you left for virtuous Jews?
moves.about: if a slave is praised as 'a good and loyal man', what praise is left for virtuous Jews
